output:
Below is a full draft you can copy into a document and sign. Two notes before you send it: fill in the year (I've left it blank), and add Darlene's last initial if your office uses full names in the file. Keep a signed copy for yourself, and save the version you hand in so you have proof of exactly what was sent to Mrs. Okafor.

---

**STATEMENT OF FACTS AND OBSERVATIONS**
**In Response to Written Complaint of October 29**

**TO:** Mrs. Okafor, Parent/Guardian of Amara Okafor, Kindergarten, Fairmont Elementary
**CC:** Darlene, Transportation Office Supervisor
**FROM:** [Your full name], School Bus Driver — Bus 41, Route 9 (Kessler Ave / Brandt St and other stops)
**RE:** Tuesday, October 27 [Year] — afternoon run — stop at Kessler Ave and Brandt St
**DATE:** November 13, [Year]

---

**Purpose of this statement**

Mrs. Okafor, I am writing this statement because the transportation office asked me to put my account of the events of Tuesday, October 27 in writing, and because I understand that a copy of it will be provided to you and placed in my personnel file. I want you to have my account directly from me, in my own words, rather than having you rely on secondhand information.

I want to begin by saying that I take your concern seriously and that I am sorry your daughter was frightened. I have grandchildren of my own, and if one of them were left standing at a stop with no adult, I would feel exactly the way you feel. That is not the reason for what happened, but it is the reason I care about this being resolved properly.

I also want to say clearly at the outset: I am not writing this to argue with you or to assign blame. My children ride school buses too, and I know how it feels to hand one of them over to someone else and hope they are looked after. I am writing to document that on October 27 I did what district procedure requires me to do, and that the actions I took were intended to protect Amara. I believe you were at that stop and waved. I do not believe you were seen that day, and I would like the record to reflect accurately where our accounts differ, because that is the only way this gets settled fairly for everybody.

**1. Summary of what happened**

On the afternoon of Tuesday, October 27, I was driving Bus 41 on Route 9. Amara Okafor was riding with me that day, as she does routinely. The stop at Kessler Ave and Brandt St is one of my assigned stops, and it is the stop where Amara is normally picked up.

I arrived at the stop at 3:52 p.m. The schedule for that run lists the Kessler stop at 3:50 p.m. I waited at the stop until approximately 3:55. During that time I did not see an adult waiting for Amara at the corner.

Amara's bag carries the green tag. Under district procedure, a green tag means an adult must be physically present at the stop for the student to be released. Because no adult was present, I was not permitted to release her. The procedure in that situation is that the student remains on the bus, the bus returns to the school, and the transportation office contacts the parent. I followed that procedure.

At 3:56 p.m. I radioed dispatch to report that I was holding at Kessler with a green-tag student and no adult present, and that I would be returning to Fairmont. Gloria, at dispatch, contacted the school to advise them of the situation.

I still had three stops to make and 14 students on the bus. I completed the remaining stops and returned to Fairmont Elementary, arriving at 4:31 p.m. I walked Amara into the school office myself and turned her over to Mrs. Petrakis in the office, so that a staff member confirmed her return.

**2. The procedure I followed, and why**

The district rule for kindergarten riders with a green tag is specific: if no adult is present at the stop, the student is not released. The student stays on the bus and is returned to the school, and the office calls the parent. That rule exists because a kindergartener cannot safely be released to an empty street corner, and because the driver's responsibility for the safety of the students aboard the bus continues until the school has custody of them.

I want to be straightforward that I am not going to apologize for following that rule, because I don't believe I did anything wrong in following it, and I don't want to leave that impression with you. But I am genuinely sorry that Amara had a bad afternoon. I understand that being on a bus that does not pull away when you expect it to, and being taken back to school, would have been confusing and upsetting for a five-year-old. There is no version of that procedure that doesn't feel a little strange to a child. I am sorry for that, and I would be sorry if it happened with my own granddaughter.

**3. Where our accounts differ**

You have told the office that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and that you waved at the bus. I want to address that directly rather than talk around it.

I did not see you. I did not see an adult at the corner at any point between 3:52 and 3:55. I want to be clear that I am not saying you weren't there. I am saying that I did not see you, and that I did not see a wave. There was a box truck parked along that side of the street, and from the driver's position the view of the far corner and of the area directly in front of the bus was substantially obstructed. It is entirely possible that you were there and that you waved and that I did not see you because of where the truck was sitting. That is a real possibility and I am not dismissing it.

That is exactly why I am asking for the camera footage to be pulled. I would rather have the video reviewed and have it confirm something that I was not able to see with my own eyes than have this decided on the basis of two people's memories of a three-minute window on a busy afternoon.

**4. Regarding your report that I "drove off laughing"**

I was not laughing. What happened is that as we pulled away from the stop, a fourth-grade student in seat 2 stood up, and I told him to sit back down. I was speaking to him. I want to state that plainly because the word "laughing" carries a meaning I don't want attached to my conduct that day. Nothing about that stop was amusing to me. The camera footage will show the front of the bus and the aisle during that moment, and it will show what my face and my attention were doing.

**5. Request that the camera footage be pulled**

I am formally requesting that the transportation office preserve and review the camera footage from Bus 41 for the afternoon run of Tuesday, October 27, 2020 [verify year], specifically the segment covering my arrival at the Kessler Ave and Brandt St stop at approximately 3:50 p.m. through my departure from that stop at approximately 3:56 p.m., and, if available, the period covering my return to Fairmont Elementary at 4:31 p.m. and the walk-in to the office.

I am requesting that this footage be retained, in case it is needed for a fuller review of the complaint, and that a copy be placed in this file and provided to me and to you. If the footage shows that I did not make the required stop, did not wait the required time, or did not return the student to the school, I would want that reviewed as well. I am asking for an honest review, not a review that supports one side.

**6. A note on why I did not get off the bus**

I understand that it may seem that I could have gotten out and walked across to the laundromat to look for you. I did not, and I would not. I had 14 kindergarten and elementary students on the bus, and I do not leave a bus with children on it to walk across a street. If I had needed to leave the bus, the correct procedure would have been to radio dispatch and request assistance, which is what I did at 3:56 p.m. No driver's concern for one student's peace of mind outweighs the safety of the students already in his care.

**7. Regarding Amara**

Amara was not distressed during the extra trip. She was coloring on her folder and she asked if she could ride some more. When I told her we were going on a little extra trip back to school, she accepted that without any fuss. I want to include this only because it is part of my account of the afternoon and it may be helpful context — not to minimize what she experienced, which I don't doubt was unsettling for her regardless of how she acted in the moment.

**8. A request going forward**

I would like to ask that when Amara is waiting for the bus, she stand on the bus side of the street where the bus stops, and that if you are in a car, you step out of the car or stand where I can clearly see you. I have no way of knowing a rider is at the corner otherwise, and on a street with parked trucks I may not see a person who is there. If I can see you, I can let you know I see you, and we can both be certain the handoff is complete. I am asking for this as a practical matter and not as a criticism of you.

**9. About my record and my continued service**

I have driven for this district for 28 years and I have no prior write-ups on my record. I am not raising that to deflect anything; I am mentioning it because I believe it is relevant to how this complaint will be weighed, and because I take the safety of the students on my bus seriously enough that I would rather be measured against the procedure than against my memory of one afternoon.

I am glad to continue driving Amara on Route 9. I would like this resolved so that neither of us is put in a position where this comes up again. I have no objection to your calling me directly at any time with a concern about the route, a stop, or Amara's care, and I would prefer that to any of this going through a file. If you believe I did something other than what I have described here, I am willing to discuss it, and I am willing to have my memory tested against the video.

**10. Closing**

I have tried to be accurate and fair in this statement, including about the parts where your account and mine differ. I followed the procedure that the district has given me for the students I am responsible for, I documented my actions to dispatch at the time, and I returned Amara to the school and into the hands of a staff member personally. I am sorry that your afternoon was worrying, and I am sorry that Amara's was too.

I am asking that the camera footage be pulled and reviewed, and I am asking that my statement be placed in the file alongside the complaint. Thank you for reading this.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[Your full name]
School Bus Driver, Bus 41, Route 9
Fairmont Elementary
[Phone number]
[Date]

**Enclosure:** Request for retention and review of Bus 41 camera footage, October 27, afternoon run.

**cc:** Darlene, Transportation Office

---

A few things I'd double-check before you turn it in: the year (I left it blank in two places so it doesn't look like a typo), whether the stop is officially "Kessler Ave and Brandt St" or just one of those names on your route sheet, and whether you want to name the fourth grader's seat number at all — I've kept it general enough that it isn't identifying. Everything else is exactly as you gave it to me.
